sentences.text: Eomamenchisaurus was a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur, a group typically defined by an extremely long neck, that lived in the Middle Jurassic of Yuanmou, Yunnan, China.

This animal is known only from a single partial skeleton, the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — which includes vertebrae, pelvic bones, and leg bones. In several respects, it displays more primitive characteristics than other members of its group.
The femur of Eomamenchisaurus is 1.1 meters long, a size similar to the femur of the 16-meter-long Mamenchisaurus youngi.
The type species E. yuanmouensis was formally described by Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2008.
Lü and colleagues originally classified Eomamenchisaurus as a mamenchisaurid.
Eomamenchisaurus lived between 174.7 and 161.5 million years ago during the Aalenian to Callovian stages.
In 2015, researchers noted that Eomamenchisaurus was difficult to distinguish from the related genus Yuanmousaurus.
